title: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi's couple (1247) and the Maragha school of astronomy
note: Ragep's MPIWG preprint dates one version to 13 February 1247 (Recension of the Almagest). Non-European contribution to the Copernican story; also expand to Ibn al-Shatir and Ali Qushji.

title: Ali Qushji, astronomer of Samarkand and Constantinople
note: Ragep's abstract credits him with a physics allowing a rotating Earth, after work at Ulugh Beg's observatory; under-recorded Central Asian scientist.

title: Roman Inquisition trial of Galileo, 1633
note: Convicted of vehement suspicion of heresy June 1633; house arrest at Arcetri. Primary trial documents are in the Vatican archives.

title: Founding of the Royal Society, London, 1660
note: Gresham College meeting 28 November 1660, charters of 1662 and 1663, Philosophical Transactions 1665 (Oldenburg).

title: De humani corporis fabrica (Vesalius, Basel, 1543)
note: Seven books, Oporinus, Basel, June or July 1543; woodcuts by Venetian artists; challenge to Galen. Wellcome and NLM hold digitised copies.

title: Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica (Newton, 1687)
note: Prompted by Halley's 1684 visit; three laws and universal gravitation; editions 1713 and 1726.

title: Jesuit astronomers at the Qing court and the transfer of European astronomy to China
note: Counterpart to the Eurocentric story of the Scientific Revolution: how the new astronomy travelled to East Asia. Dates and figures to be researched.
